operationName: Operation Swords of Iron (Israel) / October 7 War
heroHeadline: Israel's 'Orange Line' Expands Territorial Control to ~62% of Gaza; 3 Killed in May 6 Strikes
heroSubtitle: Israeli forces introduced a new restricted zone called the 'orange line' beyond the Yellow Line ceasefire boundary, with Hamas claiming Israeli control now covers approximately 62% of Gaza — up from 53% under the October 2025 ceasefire framework. The EU rejected the expansion and the UN Security Council held an emergency debate on May 5–6. Three Palestinians were killed on May 6, including a 15-year-old child struck at a northern Gaza police station, bringing deaths since the October 2025 ceasefire to approximately 832. Board of Peace envoy Mladenov reported a 'positive' meeting with Netanyahu on May 5 but acknowledged that disarmament talks remain stalled following Hamas's May 2 rejection. Two detained flotilla activists remain on hunger strike; the UN formally demanded their immediate release on May 6. Cumulative toll: 72,591+ killed since Oct 7, 2023.
footerNote: Data sourced from IDF, Hamas, UN OCHA, UNRWA, WHO, ICJ, ICC, Times of Israel, Al Jazeera, France 24, FDD/Long War Journal, NPR, and Democracy Now!. Gaza death toll: 72,591+ confirmed killed since Oct 7, 2023 (Gaza Ministry of Health / WAFA). 832+ killed since Oct 10, 2025 ceasefire framework as of May 6, 2026. Israel introduced 'orange line' expanded territorial boundary May 5–6, 2026, beyond Yellow Line ceasefire demarcation; Hamas claims Israeli control at ~62% of Gaza; EU rejected the expansion; UN Security Council debated the escalation. 3 Palestinians killed May 6 (15-year-old at northern Gaza police station; 1 in Sheikh Radwan/Gaza City airstrike; 1 by tank shelling in central Gaza). 1 killed May 5 in IDF strikes on armed cells near Yellow Line. Board of Peace envoy Mladenov met PM Netanyahu May 5; reported 'positive and substantive' discussion on Trump's 20-Point plan despite stalled Cairo talks. Hamas formally rejected UN/Board of Peace disarmament roadmap (May 2, 2026). IDF documented 19 ceasefire violations April 21–May 5. Flotilla activists Thiago Avila (Brazil) and Saif Abu Keshek (Spain) on hunger strike in Israeli custody; UN demanded immediate release (May 6). ICC arrest warrants issued for Netanyahu and Gallant (Nov 2024). Board of Peace $17B+ reconstruction fund <$1B received. EU-UN Joint Recovery and Reconstruction Assessment (Apr 21, 2026): $71.4B needed over 10 years. 2026 Flash Appeal $4.1B req, only 9.7% funded.
